queries.name: First-Time Device Logon for an Account
queries.description: Identifies users logging into a device they have never used in the past 30 days — potential lateral movement or use of stolen credentials on an unfamiliar host.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
let BaselineEnd = ago(1d);
let BaselineDevices =
    DeviceLogonEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. BaselineEnd)
    | where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
    | distinct AccountName, KnownDevice = DeviceName;
DeviceLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > BaselineEnd
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| join kind=leftouter BaselineDevices on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountName and $left.DeviceName == $right.KnownDevice
| where isempty(KnownDevice)
| project Timestamp, AccountName, DeviceName, LogonType, RemoteIP
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Generic or Shared Account Usage
queries.description: Tracks logins using shared or generic account names (administrator, admin, guest, test) that prevent individual accountability and hinder forensic investigations (T1078 — Valid Accounts).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceLogonEvents
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where AccountName in~ ("administrator", "admin", "guest", "utente", "user", "test", "default")
| summarize LoginCount = count(), Devices = dcount(DeviceName), DeviceList = make_set(DeviceName) by AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1d)
| order by LoginCount desc

queries.name: Impossible Travel — Simultaneous Logins from Different Countries
queries.description: Same account authenticated from multiple countries within the same hour — strong indicator of credential compromise since physical travel is impossible (T1078 — Valid Accounts).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceLogonEvents
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| extend Country = tostring(AdditionalFields.Country)
| where isnotempty(Country)
| summarize Countries = dcount(Country), CountryList = make_set(Country), Devices = make_set(DeviceName) by AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where Countries > 1
| order by Countries desc

queries.name: Legacy Auth MFA Bypass (Entra ID)
queries.description: Successful single-factor logins via legacy protocols (IMAP, POP3, SMTP Auth, EAS) that bypass MFA — commonly exploited in password spray attacks against Exchange Online (T1078.004 — Cloud Accounts).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
SigninLogs
| where AuthenticationRequirement == "singleFactorAuthentication"
| where ClientAppUsed in ("Exchange ActiveSync", "IMAP4", "POP3", "SMTP Auth", "Authenticated SMTP")
| where ResultType == 0
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, ClientAppUsed, AppDisplayName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

queries.name: Nighttime Logons from Named User Accounts
queries.description: Named user accounts logging in between 22:00 and 06:00 — potential unauthorized access or insider threat activity outside business hours (T1078 — Valid Accounts).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceLogonEvents
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where LogonType in ("Interactive", "RemoteInteractive", "Network")
| where hourofday(Timestamp) between (22 .. 6)
| where AccountName !startswith "svc_"
| project Timestamp, AccountName, DeviceName, LogonType, RemoteIP
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Privilege Escalation via Runas to Admin Account
queries.description: Explicit use of runas.exe to execute processes as a privileged account from a standard user — potential unauthorized escalation attempt (T1548 — Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName in~ ("runas.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/user:"
| extend TargetUser = extract(@"/user:(\S+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| where TargetUser has_any ("admin", "administrator", "domain")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, TargetUser, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: RDP Logons from Unauthorized Public IPs
queries.description: Surfaces successful Remote Desktop logons originating from public IPs not in the approved whitelist (VPN, jump hosts) — one of the most common ransomware entry vectors (T1021.001 — Remote Desktop Protocol).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceLogonEvents
| where LogonType == "RemoteInteractive"
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemoteIP !in ("0.0.0.0")
| project Timestamp, AccountName, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteIPType
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Repeated Failed Logons Followed by Success (Brute Force)
queries.description: Detects accounts with 5+ failed logon attempts followed by a successful login from the same device — classic brute force or credential stuffing pattern (T1110.001 — Brute Force).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
let FailThreshold = 5;
let failures =
    DeviceLogonEvents
    | where ActionType == "LogonFailed"
    | summarize FailCount = count(), LastFail = max(Timestamp) by AccountName, DeviceName, RemoteIP;
DeviceLogonEvents
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| join kind=inner failures on AccountName, DeviceName
| where FailCount >= FailThreshold
| project Timestamp, AccountName, DeviceName, RemoteIP, FailCount
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Service Account Interactive Logon
queries.description: Service accounts used for interactive or RDP sessions — anomalous behavior indicating abuse of technical credentials for unauthorized human access (T1078.002 — Valid Accounts: Domain Accounts).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceLogonEvents
| where LogonType in ("Interactive", "RemoteInteractive")
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where AccountName startswith "svc_" or AccountName startswith "sa_"
    or AccountName has "service" or AccountName has "svc"
| project Timestamp, AccountName, DeviceName, LogonType, RemoteIP
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Unusually Long RDP Sessions
queries.description: RDP sessions lasting more than 8 hours — potential persistent access by an external actor maintaining a foothold or using the session as a tunnel (T1021.001 — Remote Desktop Protocol).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceLogonEvents
| where LogonType == "RemoteInteractive" and ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceLogonEvents
    | where LogonType == "RemoteInteractive" and ActionType == "Logoff"
) on AccountName, DeviceName, RemoteIP
| extend SessionDurationHours = datetime_diff('hour', Timestamp1, Timestamp)
| where SessionDurationHours > 8
| project AccountName, DeviceName, RemoteIP, SessionStart = Timestamp, SessionEnd = Timestamp1, SessionDurationHours
| order by SessionDurationHours desc

queries.name: Key Vault — secret access from an anomalous IP
queries.description: Monitors secret and key reads from Key Vault, comparing the caller's IP against known IPs from the past 2 weeks. A new IP accessing Key Vault is a high-risk signal.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
let lookback  = 14d;
let recentWin = 1d;
let known_ips = AzureDiagnostics
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(lookback) .. ago(recentWin))
    | where ResourceType == "VAULTS"
    | where OperationName has_any ("SecretGet","KeyGet","CertificateGet")
    | distinct Resource, KnownCallerIPAddress = CallerIPAddress;
AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWin)
| where ResourceType == "VAULTS"
| where OperationName has_any ("SecretGet","KeyGet","CertificateGet")
| join kind=leftouter known_ips on $left.Resource == $right.Resource and $left.CallerIPAddress == $right.KnownCallerIPAddress
| where isempty(KnownCallerIPAddress)
| project TimeGenerated, Resource, OperationName,
          CallerIPAddress,
          CallerObjectId = tostring(column_ifexists("identity_claim_oid_g", column_ifexists("identity_claim_http_schemas_microsoft_com_identity_claims_objectidentifier_g", "")))

queries.name: Nuovo ruolo Owner/Contributor assegnato
queries.description: Detects the assignment of Owner or Contributor roles at the subscription or resource group level. This type of privilege escalation is a critical signal of a compromised account or misconfigured IAM.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue == "MICROSOFT.AUTHORIZATION/ROLEASSIGNMENTS/WRITE"
| where ActivityStatusValue == "Success"
| extend Props = todynamic(Properties)
| where tostring(Props.requestbody) has_any (
    "8e3af657-a8ff-443c-a75c-2fe8c4bcb635",  // Owner
    "b24988ac-6180-42a0-ab88-20f7382dd24c"   // Contributor
  )
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress,
          ResourceGroup, SubscriptionId

queries.name: Resource Group Deletion — cancellazioni massicce
queries.description: Detects successfully completed resource group deletion operations. Deleting entire RGs may indicate destructive post-compromise activity or serious operational errors.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OperationNameValue == "MICROSOFT.RESOURCES/SUBSCRIPTIONS/RESOURCEGROUPS/DELETE"
| where ActivityStatusValue == "Succeeded"
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress,
          ResourceGroup, SubscriptionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

queries.name: WAF Firewall Events — Detailed by Client IP and URI
queries.description: Aggregates Azure Application Gateway WAF firewall log entries by client IP, request URI, WAF action, site, and rule details. Useful for identifying blocked attacks and false positives per minute.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AzureDiagnostics
| where ResourceProvider == "MICROSOFT.NETWORK"
    and Category == "ApplicationGatewayFirewallLog"
| summarize count() by clientIp_s, requestUri_s, action_s, site_s, details_message_s, details_data_s, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)

queries.name: WAF Firewall Events — Top Blocked Client IPs and URIs
queries.description: Summarizes WAF events by client IP and requested URI to identify the most frequently triggered sources and endpoints. Helps prioritize IP blocking and WAF rule tuning.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AzureDiagnostics
| where ResourceProvider == "MICROSOFT.NETWORK"
    and Category == "ApplicationGatewayFirewallLog"
| summarize count() by clientIp_s, requestUri_s
| sort by count_ desc

queries.name: NSG Flow Logs — Complete Traffic Analysis
queries.description: Parses AzureNetworkAnalytics_CL flow logs to surface direction, access decision, protocol, source/destination IPs and ports, and the matching NSG rule. Filter by DestIP to scope to a specific subnet.
queries.mitreNotApplicable: Generic NSG flow log traffic analysis
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AzureNetworkAnalytics_CL
| where SubType_s == "FlowLog"
| extend Direction = case(FlowDirection_s == "O", "Outbound", FlowDirection_s == "I", "Inbound", FlowDirection_s)
| extend Access = case(FlowStatus_s == 'A', 'Allowed', FlowStatus_s == 'D', 'Denied', FlowStatus_s)
| extend Protocol = case(L4Protocol_s == "T", "TCP", L4Protocol_s == "U", "UDP", L4Protocol_s)
| project TimeGenerated, Direction, Access, SrcIP_s, DestIP_s, DestPort_d, Protocol, L7Protocol_s, NSGRule_s
| where DestIP_s contains "172.168.0." // replace with your target subnet

queries.name: NSG Flow Logs — Filter by Specific Public IP
queries.description: Returns all NSG flow log entries where the Public IP matches a specific address. Use during incident response to identify all traffic associated with a known malicious or suspicious IP.
queries.mitreNotApplicable: Generic IOC pivot on a single IP
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AzureNetworkAnalytics_CL
| where SubType_s == "FlowLog"
| where PublicIPs_s contains "62.180.229.43" // replace with the IP to investigate

queries.name: NSG — Inbound Traffic for Specific Resource
queries.description: Returns all inbound NSG flow entries for a specific network security group resource. Replace the Resource filter with your NSG name. Useful for reviewing allowed and denied inbound traffic.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AzureDiagnostics
| where ResourceType == "NETWORKSECURITYGROUPS"
    and Resource contains "vnet-nsg-ftp" // replace with your NSG resource name
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where direction_s == "In"

queries.name: Agent 365 — Active AI agent inventory
queries.description: Lists the current inventory of active (non-deleted) agents registered through Agent 365. Use this as the baseline inventory before assessing agent risk posture. Review CreatorAccountUpn to understand who is building agents and whether agent creation aligns with organizational policy. Empty results indicate no Agent 365 agents are deployed — also a useful data point when auditing the agentic surface.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AIAgentsInfo
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AIAgentId
| where RegistrySource == "A365"
| where AgentStatus != "Deleted"

queries.name: Agent 365 — Agents with MCP tool configured (expanded attack surface)
queries.description: Identifies AI agents that have Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool configurations, which give them the ability to invoke external tool operations and expand their attack surface beyond standard agent interactions. Lists configured MCP tool names grouped by agent and creator. Review tool names and creator accounts to determine whether configurations are authorized. An unrecognized MCP tool warrants investigation into what it accesses and who approved its configuration.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AIAgentsInfo
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AIAgentId
| where AgentStatus != "Deleted"
| mvexpand Action = AgentToolsDetails
| where Action.action.operationDetails["$kind"] == "ModelContextProtocolMetadata"
| extend MCPName = Action.action.operationDetails["operationId"]
| summarize MCPTools = make_set(MCPName)
  by AIAgentName, AIAgentId, EnvironmentId, CreatorAccountUpn

queries.name: Agent 365 — Agents without user authentication (security hygiene)
queries.description: Finds agents with UserAuthenticationType == "None", meaning they accept interactions without authenticating the caller. Activity from these agents cannot be reliably attributed to a specific identity. Review creator and owner accounts to determine whether missing authentication is intentional (e.g., a public FAQ bot) or an oversight. For agents that handle sensitive data or perform actions on behalf of users, missing authentication is a risk to escalate to the agent owner for remediation.
queries.mitreNotApplicable: AI agent security hygiene posture check
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AIAgentsInfo
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AIAgentId
| where AgentStatus != "Deleted"
| where UserAuthenticationType == "None"
| project AIAgentName, AIAgentId, CreatorAccountUpn,
          OwnerAccountUpns, UserAuthenticationType, AgentCreationTime

queries.name: Azure AI Agent — Access from anonymized IP (Tor / anonymizer, preview)
queries.description: Identifies Defender for Cloud AI agent alerts where the access originates from an anonymizing network such as Tor. High severity. Preview signal. Access to AI agents from anonymizing networks is a strong indicator of intentional evasion. Investigate whether the actor is an authenticated user and escalate if access involved sensitive data or privileged agent operations.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
SecurityAlert
| where AlertType in ("AI.Azure_Agentic_AccessFromAnonymizedIP")
       or AlertName in ("AI.Azure_Agentic_AccessFromAnonymizedIP")
| project TimeGenerated, AlertName, AlertType, Severity,
          Description, Entities, ExtendedProperties

queries.name: Azure AI Agent — Access from suspicious IP (threat intelligence, preview)
queries.description: Surfaces Defender for Cloud AI agent alerts where the access originates from an IP address flagged by Microsoft threat intelligence as suspicious. High severity. Preview signal. Correlate with identity telemetry (Entra SigninLogs) to determine whether the IP is associated with a known threat actor, VPN abuse, or compromised infrastructure.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
SecurityAlert
| where AlertType in ("AI.Azure_Agentic_AccessFromSuspiciousIP")
       or AlertName in ("AI.Azure_Agentic_AccessFromSuspiciousIP")
| project TimeGenerated, AlertName, AlertType, Severity,
          Description, Entities, ExtendedProperties

queries.name: Azure AI Agent — Access from suspicious user agent (preview)
queries.description: Surfaces Defender for Cloud AI agent alerts where the HTTP user-agent string is suspicious — for example, automated tooling, scrapers, or known attack frameworks. High severity. Preview signal. Suspicious user agents accessing AI agents may indicate automated abuse, credential stuffing, or reconnaissance. Review ExtendedProperties for the raw user-agent string.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
SecurityAlert
| where AlertType in ("AI.Azure_Agentic_AccessFromSuspiciousUserAgent")
       or AlertName in ("AI.Azure_Agentic_AccessFromSuspiciousUserAgent")
| project TimeGenerated, AlertName, AlertType, Severity,
          Description, Entities, ExtendedProperties

queries.name: Azure AI Agent — ASCII smuggling detected (preview)
queries.description: Surfaces Defender for Cloud AI agent alerts indicating ASCII smuggling attempts, a technique where hidden or obfuscated characters are embedded in prompts to bypass content filters or covertly exfiltrate data. High severity. Preview signal — may fire at lower volume until the detection matures. Investigate Entities and ExtendedProperties for the affected resource and actor context.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
SecurityAlert
| where AlertType in ("AI.Azure_Agentic_ASCIISmuggling")
       or AlertName in ("AI.Azure_Agentic_ASCIISmuggling")
| project TimeGenerated, AlertName, AlertType, Severity,
          Description, Entities, ExtendedProperties

queries.name: Azure AI Agent — Jailbreak attempt detected by Prompt Shields (preview)
queries.description: Identifies Defender for Cloud AI agent alerts where Prompt Shields detected (but may not have blocked) a jailbreak attempt against an agentic workflow. Medium severity. Preview signal — distinct from the blocked-jailbreak variant in that the attempt was detected without necessarily being stopped. Correlate with the agent inventory queries (copilotai-9 through copilotai-11) to assess the agent's risk posture and authorization configuration.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
SecurityAlert
| where AlertType in ("AI.Azure_Agentic_Jailbreak")
       or AlertName in ("AI.Azure_Agentic_Jailbreak")
| project TimeGenerated, AlertName, AlertType, Severity,
          Description, Entities, ExtendedProperties

queries.name: Azure AI Agent — Malicious URL via user prompt detected (preview)
queries.description: Identifies Defender for Cloud AI agent alerts where a phishing or malicious URL was provided to an AI agent through a user prompt. High severity. The agent may follow the URL as part of tool use, enabling data exfiltration or redirection attacks. Preview signal. Review Entities for the user and resource involved and block the actor if confirmed malicious.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
SecurityAlert
| where AlertType in ("AI.Azure_Agentic_MaliciousUrl.UserPrompt")
       or AlertName in ("AI.Azure_Agentic_MaliciousUrl.UserPrompt")
| project TimeGenerated, AlertName, AlertType, Severity,
          Description, Entities, ExtendedProperties

queries.name: Azure AI — Credential theft and jailbreak alerts (Defender for Cloud)
queries.description: Queries Defender for Cloud alerts specific to Azure AI services: credential theft attempts (credentials appeared in a model response) and jailbreak attempts blocked or detected by content filtering. These are higher-confidence signals than the M365 Copilot JailbreakDetected flag. Review Entities and ExtendedProperties for resource identifiers and actor details. Credential theft alerts are urgent — a model leaking credentials is an active exposure. Pivot to the Azure Activity correlation query to check for follow-on deployment or key-listing operations.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
SecurityAlert
| where AlertType in (
    "AI.Azure_CredentialTheftAttempt",
    "AI.Azure_Jailbreak.ContentFiltering.BlockedAttempt",
    "AI.Azure_Jailbreak.ContentFiltering.DetectedAttempt"
  )
| project TimeGenerated, AlertName, AlertType, Severity,
          Description, Entities, ExtendedProperties

queries.name: Azure AI — Credential theft correlated with Azure Activity (deployment/listKeys pattern)
queries.description: Joins Azure AI credential theft alerts with Azure Activity operations — specifically Cognitive Services account deployment writes and listKeys actions — within a one-hour window. A credential theft alert followed by a listKeys action suggests potential exploitation: the attacker may have used credentials from the model response to access the Azure AI resource directly. If no matching activity is found, remediate the exposed credentials regardless. Expand the join window if your environment has higher ingestion latency.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
let AiAlerts = SecurityAlert
| where AlertType == "AI.Azure_CredentialTheftAttempt"
| project AlertTime = TimeGenerated, AlertName, AlertType,
          Severity, Entities, ExtendedProperties;
AiAlerts
| join kind=leftouter (
    AzureActivity
    | where OperationNameValue in (
        "Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/write",
        "Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/listKeys/action"
      )
    | project ActivityTime = TimeGenerated, OperationNameValue,
              Caller, ResourceGroup, ResourceId
  )
  on $left.AlertTime between ($right.ActivityTime .. $right.ActivityTime + 1h)

queries.name: Copilot — Baseline activity by user (Who / When / Where)
queries.description: Returns a chronological view of all M365 Copilot activity for a specific user, including which application hosted the interaction and when it occurred. Use this as the starting point to establish the time window and application scope under investigation. Multiple AppHost values indicate usage spanning several workloads. Narrow the time range and pivot to resource-expansion queries to determine what Copilot accessed.
queries.mitreNotApplicable: Per-user Copilot activity timeline for investigation scoping
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CopilotActivity
| where ActorName == "user@domain.com"   // replace with target UPN
| project TimeGenerated, ActorName, AppHost, RecordType, OrganizationId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

queries.name: Copilot — Expand accessed resources (blast-radius / Contexts)
queries.description: Expands the Contexts array inside LLMEventData to enumerate every resource M365 Copilot accessed during each interaction. Each row is a single resource (file, email, calendar item, etc.) with its identifier and type. Use this to determine the blast radius of an interaction: which data sources were referenced. Cross-reference resource identifiers with DLP or data classification systems to assess sensitivity.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CopilotActivity
| extend Contexts = parse_json(LLMEventData.Contexts)
| mv-expand ctx = Contexts
| extend ResourceId   = tostring(ctx.Id),
         ResourceType = tostring(ctx.Type)
| project TimeGenerated, ActorName, AppHost, ResourceId, ResourceType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

queries.name: Copilot — High-volume usage anomaly (>50 events/hour per user)
queries.description: Identifies users generating more than 50 M365 Copilot events in a single hour, flagging statistical outliers that may warrant investigation. High volume alone is not evidence of abuse — legitimate power users, automated workflows, or testing can produce similar patterns. Triage by examining AppHost and resource context to determine whether the volume reflects normal work or anomalous behavior. Adjust the threshold to match your organization's baseline usage.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CopilotActivity
| summarize EventCount = count() by ActorName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where EventCount > 50
| order by EventCount desc

queries.name: Copilot — Investigator export view (evidence case packet)
queries.description: Produces a structured export of M365 Copilot activity combining user identity, source IP, application context, and accessed resources — suitable as the evidence foundation for a case file. Captures metadata from the CopilotActivity table. Note: audit logs are metadata-first and do not contain the actual text of prompts or responses. When content-level evidence is required (what was asked / what was returned), pivot to Microsoft Purview eDiscovery or DSPM for AI.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CopilotActivity
| extend Contexts     = parse_json(LLMEventData.Contexts)
| mv-expand ctx       = Contexts
| extend ResourceId   = tostring(ctx.Id),
         ResourceType = tostring(ctx.Type)
| project TimeGenerated, ActorName, ActorUserId, SrcIpAddr,
          AppHost, ResourceId, ResourceType, RecordType

queries.name: Copilot — JailbreakDetected signals in message metadata
queries.description: Surfaces M365 Copilot interactions where the built-in safety system flagged a user prompt as a potential jailbreak attempt (JailbreakDetected == true). This is a detection signal, not a confirmed attack — false positives occur. Evaluate in context: a single flagged event from a curious user differs from repeated attempts by the same actor across multiple AppHost values. Sustained or escalating patterns warrant correlation with Azure AI alert queries and potential escalation.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CopilotActivity
| extend Messages          = parse_json(LLMEventData.Messages)
| mv-expand msg            = Messages
| extend JailbreakDetected = tobool(msg.JailbreakDetected)
| where JailbreakDetected == true
| project TimeGenerated, ActorName, AppHost, JailbreakDetected

queries.name: Defender XDR — AI-related alerts sweep (AlertInfo + AlertEvidence join)
queries.description: Broad sweep across Defender XDR alerts matching AI threat keywords: Jailbreak, prompt injection, credential theft. Returns alerts with associated evidence entities (users, IPs, resources) from AlertEvidence. Use this for a cross-product view of AI-related alerts rather than targeting a specific alert type. Review AttackTechniques for MITRE mapping. If the result set is large, narrow by Severity or ServiceSource to prioritize triage.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AlertInfo
| where Title has_any ("Jailbreak", "prompt injection", "credential theft")
| project Timestamp, AlertId, Title, Category, Severity,
          ServiceSource, DetectionSource, AttackTechniques
| join kind=leftouter (
    AlertEvidence
    | project AlertId, EntityType, EntityValue
  ) on AlertId

queries.name: Bulk Cloud Download (Pre-Exfiltration Staging)
queries.description: More than 200 downloads from any cloud app in one hour — typical pre-exfiltration pattern where a user bulk-collects from M365 before uploading to personal storage (T1530 — Data from Cloud Storage).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType in ("FileDownloaded", "Download")
| summarize
    DownloadCount = count(),
    Apps = make_set(Application),
    Files = make_set(ObjectName, 20)
    by AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where DownloadCount > 200
| order by DownloadCount desc

queries.name: Bulk External Upload (Mass Exfiltration)
queries.description: More than 20 file uploads to non-Microsoft cloud services in one hour — calibrate threshold to your baseline; high values almost always indicate intentional exfiltration (T1030 — Data Transfer Size Limits).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "FileUploaded"
| where Application !in ("Microsoft SharePoint Online", "Microsoft OneDrive", "Microsoft Teams")
| summarize
    UploadCount = count(),
    Apps = make_set(Application),
    Files = make_set(ObjectName, 20),
    TotalSizeMB = sum(todouble(AdditionalFields.FileSize)) / 1048576
    by AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where UploadCount > 20
| order by UploadCount desc

queries.name: Cloud App Access from Unexpected Country
queries.description: Access to cloud apps from countries outside the approved policy list — potential compromised account using valid credentials bypassing corporate infrastructure. Adapt the country list.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where Application in (
    "Dropbox", "Box", "Google Drive", "Slack",
    "ChatGPT", "OpenAI", "WeTransfer", "Trello", "Notion"
)
| where CountryCode !in ("IT", "US", "GB", "DE", "FR") // adapt to your policy
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, Application, ActionType, IPAddress, CountryCode, ISP
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Cloud App Access from Unmanaged Device
queries.description: Access to unapproved cloud services from a device not enrolled in Intune — high-risk combination: corporate data transiting outside IT-controlled infrastructure (T1078.004 — Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where Application in ("Dropbox", "Box", "Google Drive", "ChatGPT", "OpenAI", "WeTransfer")
| where AdditionalFields has "UnmanagedDevice"
    or AdditionalFields has "Compliant:No"
    or AdditionalFields has "ManagedDevice:No"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, Application, ActionType, IPAddress, CountryCode, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Custom Privileged RBAC Role Created in Entra ID
queries.description: Custom RBAC role definitions with elevated permissions created in Entra ID — stealth persistence technique that avoids monitoring on well-known built-in roles (T1098.003).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName == "Add custom role definition to a role management policy"
    or OperationName == "Add role definition"
| extend CreatedBy = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend RoleName = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| project TimeGenerated, CreatedBy, RoleName, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

queries.name: Dynamic Group Membership Rules Modified
queries.description: Changes to Entra ID dynamic group membership rules can silently include unintended users in groups that grant access to sensitive resources.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName == "Update group"
| where TargetResources has "membershipRule"
| extend ModifiedBy = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend OldRule = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].modifiedProperties[0].oldValue)
| extend NewRule = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].modifiedProperties[0].newValue)
| project TimeGenerated, ModifiedBy, OldRule, NewRule
| order by TimeGenerated desc

queries.name: External Guest User Added to Teams or M365 Group
queries.description: B2B guest accounts added to internal groups may expose documents and channels to unverified third parties — particularly risky when groups contain sensitive project data (T1136.003 — Cloud Account).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "Add member to group."
| where AdditionalFields has "#EXT#"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AdditionalFields, IPAddress, Application
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: File Upload to Unapproved External Cloud Storage
queries.description: File uploads to personal or unapproved cloud storage (Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, Mega, etc.) — classic insider threat or compromised account exfiltration vector (T1567.002 — Exfiltration to Cloud Storage).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "FileUploaded"
| where Application in (
    "Dropbox", "Box", "Google Drive", "WeTransfer",
    "Mega", "pCloud", "iCloud Drive", "Sync.com",
    "MediaFire", "Zippyshare"
)
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, Application, ObjectName, IPAddress, CountryCode, ISP
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Files Uploaded to AI Platforms (Data Leakage via Prompt)
queries.description: Direct file uploads to generative AI services — corporate documents, contracts, or source code uploaded as prompt context represent an immediate and difficult-to-reverse DLP risk.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where Application in (
    "ChatGPT", "OpenAI", "Google Gemini", "Claude",
    "Perplexity AI", "Mistral AI", "Hugging Face"
)
| where ActionType in ("FileUploaded", "Upload", "Attach")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, Application, ActionType, ObjectName, IPAddress
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Group Permission Scope Expansion
queries.description: Modifications enabling external senders, auto-subscription, or public visibility on distribution or unified groups — potential data exfiltration channel.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType in ("Update group.", "Set-UnifiedGroup", "Set-DistributionGroup")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("AccessType", "AllowExternalSenders", "AutoSubscribeNewMembers", "HiddenFromAddressListsEnabled")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, ActionType, AdditionalFields, IPAddress
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: M365 / Teams Group Created by Non-IT User
queries.description: Non-IT users creating Teams or Microsoft 365 groups can establish shadow IT, uncontrolled data sharing, or channels used for exfiltration.
queries.mitreNotApplicable: Shadow-IT governance check on group creation
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType in ("Add group.", "Create group")
| where Application in ("Microsoft Teams", "Office 365")
| where AccountDisplayName !in ("IT Admin", "M365 Admin")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, ActionType, AdditionalFields, IPAddress
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Privileged Role Assignment in Entra ID
queries.description: Every assignment of a high-privilege Entra ID role should be correlated with a change management ticket — unplanned assignments are a common persistence technique (T1098.003).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName == "Add member to role."
| extend AssignedBy = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend TargetUser = tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName)
| extend RoleName = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| where RoleName has_any ("Global Administrator", "Security Administrator", "Exchange Administrator", "SharePoint Administrator")
| project TimeGenerated, AssignedBy, TargetUser, RoleName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

queries.name: Public File Sharing on Dropbox or Box
queries.description: Files shared via public or anonymous links on external cloud storage — severe DLP violation as data exits the M365 perimeter and is beyond native Microsoft monitoring controls.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where Application in ("Dropbox", "Box", "Google Drive")
| where ActionType in ("SharedLink", "SharedLinkCreated", "SharingSet", "FileShared")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("public", "anyone", "open", "anonymous")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, Application, ActionType, ObjectName, AdditionalFields, IPAddress
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Shadow AI Usage (Unapproved Generative AI Services)
queries.description: Access to generative AI services not approved by policy — risk of data leakage via prompts containing confidential data, source code, or customer information (Shadow AI / T1567).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where Application in (
    "ChatGPT", "OpenAI", "Google Bard", "Google Gemini",
    "Perplexity AI", "Claude", "Mistral AI", "Cohere",
    "Hugging Face", "Character.AI", "Poe", "Jasper",
    "Copy.ai", "Writesonic", "Midjourney", "Stable Diffusion Online"
)
| where ActionType in ("Login", "Upload", "FileUploaded", "QuerySent", "MessageSent")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, Application, ActionType, ObjectName, IPAddress, CountryCode
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Teams External Federation or Shared Channels Enabled
queries.description: Settings enabling Teams consumer federation or shared channels with external tenants — if unplanned, can open internal data to unauthorized organizations.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "TeamsTenantSettingChanged"
    or ActionType == "ExternalAccessSettingChanged"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("AllowTeamsConsumer", "AllowFederatedUsers", "SharedChannels")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, ActionType, AdditionalFields, IPAddress
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Anomalous Parent-Child Process Chain (Process Injection)
queries.description: Critical system processes (svchost, lsass, winlogon) spawning unexpected children — indicator of process injection or process hollowing where attacker code runs inside a trusted host (T1055 — Process Injection).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("svchost.exe", "lsass.exe", "winlogon.exe", "csrss.exe", "smss.exe")
| where FileName !in~ (
    "conhost.exe", "WerFault.exe", "wermgr.exe",
    "WmiPrvSE.exe", "taskhost.exe", "taskhostw.exe"
)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Application Config Files Modified
queries.description: Modifications to application configuration files (web.config, appsettings.json, .env, wp-config.php) — used to inject C2 connections, change DB credentials, or disable security controls (T1565 — Data Manipulation).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType in ("FileModified", "FileCreated")
| where FileName in~ ("web.config", "appsettings.json", "config.xml", ".env", "wp-config.php", "settings.py")
| extend AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Certutil Used as Downloader (LOLBin Abuse)
queries.description: certutil.exe invoked with download flags (-urlcache, -f, -split) and HTTP URLs — Living-off-the-Land Binary abuse to fetch payloads while bypassing proxy and AV controls (T1140 — Deobfuscate/Decode).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "certutil.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-urlcache", "-f", "-split", "-decode")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "http"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Credential File Access by Unexpected Process
queries.description: Reads of password manager databases, certificate files, or files containing "password" or "credential" by processes other than known password managers — local credential harvesting (T1555 — Credentials from Password Stores).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType == "FileRead"
| where FileName endswith ".kdbx" or FileName has "password"
    or FileName has "credential" or FileName has "wallet"
    or FileName endswith ".pfx" or FileName endswith ".p12"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("keepass.exe", "1password.exe", "bitwarden.exe")
| extend AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Critical Windows System Files Modified or Deleted
queries.description: Modifications to critical system files (lsass.exe, svchost.exe, hosts, ntoskrnl.exe) in System32/SysWOW64 — tampering technique for persistence or network redirection (T1565.001 — Stored Data Manipulation).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType in ("FileModified", "FileRenamed", "FileDeleted")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"C:\Windows\System32\", @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64\")
| where FileName in~ ("hosts", "lsass.exe", "svchost.exe", "ntoskrnl.exe", "winlogon.exe")
| extend AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Cross-User File Access (Privilege Abuse)
queries.description: A user reading files under another user's profile directory — may indicate elevated privilege abuse or a compromised admin account browsing sensitive data (T1083 — File and Directory Discovery).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType == "FileRead"
| where FolderPath has @"C:\Users\"
| extend PathOwner = tostring(split(FolderPath, @"\")[2])
| extend AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where PathOwner != AccountName
| where PathOwner !in~ ("Public", "Default", "All Users")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, PathOwner, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Double-Extension Files Downloaded by Browser
queries.description: Flags browser-downloaded files matching a double-extension pattern (e.g. invoice.pdf.exe) — a social engineering technique to disguise executables as harmless documents.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe", "iexplore.exe")
| where FileName matches regex @"\.(doc|xls|pdf|zip)\.(exe|bat|vbs|js|ps1)$"
| extend AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Executables Created in User-Writable Folders
queries.description: Dropper or malware stages executables in user-accessible folders (Temp, ProgramData, Users) to avoid detection in monitored system directories (T1204.002 — User Execution: Malicious File).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"C:\Users\", @"C:\ProgramData\", @"C:\Temp\", @"C:\Windows\Temp\")
| where FileName endswith ".exe" or FileName endswith ".dll"
    or FileName endswith ".bat" or FileName endswith ".ps1"
| extend AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: File Hash IOC Matching (Threat Intelligence)
queries.description: Matches created files against known malicious SHA256 hashes from threat intelligence. Feed this query with a Sentinel Watchlist of current IOCs for production use (T1204 — User Execution).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where SHA256 in (
    "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855",
    "aec070645fe53ee3b3763059376134f058cc337247c978add178b6ccdfb0019f"
)
| extend AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Files Copied to Removable USB Drives
queries.description: File copy or creation events targeting removable drive letters — classic insider threat data exfiltration vector via physical media (T1052.001 — Exfiltration Over Physical Medium: Exfiltration over USB).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType == "FileCopied"
    or (ActionType == "FileCreated" and (FolderPath startswith @"E:\" or FolderPath startswith @"F:\"))
| extend AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Interactive Logons Outside Working Hours
queries.description: Surfaces interactive and RDP logons occurring outside 07:00–19:00 on weekdays or on weekends — a signal for unauthorized physical or remote access (T1078 — Valid Accounts).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceLogonEvents
| where LogonType in ("Interactive", "RemoteInteractive")
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where hourofday(Timestamp) !between (7 .. 19)
    or dayofweek(Timestamp) in (0d, 6d) // Sunday, Saturday
| summarize LogonCount = count() by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where LogonCount >= 1
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Known Hacking Tools Executed by Name
queries.description: Execution of well-known post-exploitation tools (Mimikatz, BloodHound, Rubeus, Impacket, CrackMapExec, etc.) — near-certain true positives requiring immediate response (T1003 — OS Credential Dumping).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName in~ (
    "mimikatz.exe", "procdump.exe", "wce.exe", "fgdump.exe",
    "pwdump.exe", "lazagne.exe", "sharphound.exe", "bloodhound.exe",
    "rubeus.exe", "kerbrute.exe", "impacket.exe", "crackmapexec.exe"
)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Lateral Movement — PsExec e WMI remoto
queries.description: Identifies lateral connections via PsExec, WMI, or remote administration tools. Shows source-destination pairs with timestamps to map the attacker's progression through the network.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("PsExec.exe","PsExec64.exe","wmic.exe","winrm.cmd")
    or (InitiatingProcessFileName == "svchost.exe"
        and RemotePort in (135, 445, 5985, 5986))
| summarize
    Connections  = count(),
    Destinations = make_set(RemoteIP, 20)
  by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where Connections > 2
| order by Connections desc

queries.name: LOLBIN — Living Off the Land Binaries sospetti
queries.description: Detects the use of legitimate Windows binaries (certutil, mshta, wscript, regsvr32, rundll32) with arguments typical of remote download or execution, a classic technique to evade AV/EDR solutions.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
let lolbins = dynamic([
    "certutil.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
    "regsvr32.exe","rundll32.exe","msiexec.exe","bitsadmin.exe"
]);
let suspicious_args = dynamic([
    "http","ftp","\\","urlcache","download",
    "scrobj","javascript","vbscript"
]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where FileName in~ (lolbins)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (suspicious_args)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName

queries.name: Long Base64 Strings in Process Arguments
queries.description: Command lines containing Base64 strings longer than 100 characters — obfuscation technique to hide malicious commands from static analysis and AV signature detection (T1027 — Obfuscated Files or Information).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"[A-Za-z0-9+/]{100,}={0,2}"
| where FileName !in~ ("java.exe", "node.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: LSASS Credential Dump via CreateRemoteThread
queries.description: Detects remote thread injection into lsass.exe — the standard technique used by Mimikatz and similar tools to extract password hashes from memory (T1003.001 — OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "CreateRemoteThreadApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Mass File Deletion — Sabotage or Pre-Ransomware
queries.description: More than 200 files deleted within 10 minutes — can precede ransomware (shadow copy deletion) or be deliberate sabotage by an insider threat (T1485 — Data Destruction).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType == "FileDeleted"
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| extend AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| summarize DeletedCount = count(), Extensions = make_set(tostring(split(FileName, ".")[-1])) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where DeletedCount > 200
| order by DeletedCount desc

queries.name: Mass File Rename — Ransomware Early Indicator
queries.description: Detects a high volume of file renames within 10-minute windows — an early ransomware indicator as files are renamed in bulk during the encryption phase (T1486 — Data Encrypted for Impact).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType == "FileRenamed"
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| extend AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| summarize RenamedFiles = count(), Extensions = make_set(tostring(split(FileName, ".")[-1])) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where RenamedFiles > 100
| order by RenamedFiles desc

queries.name: Network Connections to Known C2 Ports
queries.description: Identifies outbound connections to ports associated with attack frameworks such as Metasploit or Cobalt Strike (4444, 1234, 8080, 9001, 9002, 31337). Public IP filter reduces noise from internal services.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where RemotePort in (4444, 1234, 8080, 9001, 9002, 31337)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Non-Browser Processes Spawning Internet Connections
queries.description: Joins process and network events to identify non-browser, non-standard processes opening public internet connections — detection pattern for backdoors and RATs communicating with C2 (T1071 — Application Layer Protocol).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
    | where RemoteIPType == "Public"
) on DeviceId, $left.ProcessId == $right.InitiatingProcessId
| where FileName !in~ ("chrome.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe", "outlook.exe", "teams.exe", "svchost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Office Apps Spawning Anomalous Child Processes
queries.description: Detects Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) launching shell interpreters as child processes — a strong indicator of malicious macros or armed documents attempting to execute code (T1566.001 — Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe", "excel.exe", "outlook.exe", "mspub.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "mshta.exe", "regsvr32.exe", "rundll32.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: PowerShell — Comandi encoded sospetti
queries.description: Detects PowerShell executions using the -EncodedCommand flag or equivalent abbreviations, commonly used to obfuscate malicious payloads and bypass keyword-based detection rules.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-EncodedCommand", "-Enc ", "-ec ", " -e ")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msiexec.exe","svchost.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

queries.name: PowerShell — Potential Download Activity
queries.description: Detects PowerShell processes that reference download-related .NET classes or HTTP strings (WebClient, DownloadFile, DownloadString, WebRequest). Correlates both process and network events to catch first-stage downloaders that pull a second payload from the internet.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
union DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","powershell_ise.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any("WebClient","DownloadFile","DownloadString","WebRequest","http")

queries.name: Privilege Escalation via Token Impersonation
queries.description: Detects token impersonation events involving SeImpersonatePrivilege or SeDebugPrivilege — used to escalate to SYSTEM or other privileged contexts post-compromise (T1134 — Access Token Manipulation).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "TokenImpersonation"
| where AdditionalFields has "SeImpersonatePrivilege"
    or AdditionalFields has "SeDebugPrivilege"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Processes Launched from Temp or User Folders
queries.description: Executables launched from Temp, AppData, or public user folders — staging pattern used by malware that avoids monitored system directories during initial execution (T1204.002 — Malicious File).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath has_any (@"C:\Temp\", @"C:\Windows\Temp\", @"C:\Users\Public\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| where FileName endswith ".exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Processes with Hidden Window (Stealth Execution)
queries.description: Processes launched with hidden window flags (-WindowStyle Hidden, -w hidden, CreateNoWindow) — stealth execution technique used by malware and malicious PowerShell scripts to avoid user awareness (T1564.003 — Hide Artifacts: Hidden Window).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where AdditionalFields has "WindowStyle:Hidden"
    or ProcessCommandLine has "-WindowStyle Hidden"
    or ProcessCommandLine has "-w hidden"
    or ProcessCommandLine has "CreateNoWindow"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: PsExec / Remote Admin Tool Execution
queries.description: Detects execution of PsExec and similar remote administration tools commonly used for lateral movement over SMB admin shares (T1021.002 — Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe", "psexec64.exe", "paexec.exe", "remcom.exe", "csexec.exe")
    or ProcessCommandLine has @"\\admin$"
    or ProcessCommandLine has @"\\ipc$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Repeated Failed Logon Attempts (Aggregated)
queries.description: Uses the LogonFailedAggregatedReport action type to surface devices with more than 10 unique failed logon events over 30 days. The aggregated report is less noisy than raw events and is useful for spotting persistent brute-force activity or misconfigured services.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "LogonFailedAggregatedReport"
| extend n = toint(todynamic(AdditionalFields).uniqueEventsAggregated)
| where n > 10
| sort by n desc

queries.name: Scheduled Task sospetto creato da processo insolito
queries.description: Finds scheduled tasks created by processes not typically responsible for this operation (PowerShell, cmd, wscript). Common persistence technique on compromised endpoints.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where FileName == "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (
    "powershell.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
    "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe"
  )
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine

queries.name: Scheduled Tasks Created by Non-System Accounts
queries.description: schtasks.exe or at.exe creating new tasks from non-system accounts — classic post-compromise persistence mechanism to ensure malware re-executes after reboot (T1053.005 — Scheduled Task).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName in~ ("schtasks.exe", "at.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create" or ProcessCommandLine has "-create"
| where AccountName !in~ ("SYSTEM", "LOCAL SERVICE", "NETWORK SERVICE")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Script Execution via mshta, wscript, or cscript with URLs
queries.description: mshta.exe, wscript.exe, or cscript.exe invoked with HTA/VBS/JS files or remote URLs — common first-stage dropper vector distributed via phishing attachments (T1059.005 — Visual Basic).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName in~ ("mshta.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".hta", ".vbs", ".js", "http://", "https://", "ftp://")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Scripts Written to Disk by Non-Editor Processes
queries.description: Script files (.ps1, .bat, .vbs, .js) created by processes other than known editors — multi-stage dropper pattern where the first stage materializes subsequent payloads on disk (T1059 — Command and Scripting Interpreter).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName endswith ".ps1" or FileName endswith ".bat"
    or FileName endswith ".vbs" or FileName endswith ".js"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("code.exe", "notepad.exe", "notepad++.exe", "explorer.exe")
| extend AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Suspicious RDP Connections (Port 3389 Aggregated)
queries.description: Surfaces devices with more than 10 aggregated inbound or outbound RDP connections on port 3389. Uses the AggregatedReport action type to reduce noise while still flagging endpoints with unusual Remote Desktop activity, a common ransomware entry vector.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ActionType endswith "AggregatedReport" and RemotePort == "3389"
| extend n = toint(todynamic(AdditionalFields).uniqueEventsAggregated)
| where n > 10
| sort by n desc

queries.name: Symbolic Link or Junction Point Creation to Protected Folders
queries.description: Use of mklink or New-Item SymbolicLink targeting system directories — technique used for privilege escalation or bypassing file access controls (T1574 — Hijack Execution Flow).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "mklink"
    or (ProcessCommandLine has "New-Item" and ProcessCommandLine has "SymbolicLink")
    or ProcessCommandLine has "junction"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Windows Defender Disabled or Modified via Registry
queries.description: Detects registry modifications that disable Windows Defender real-time protection or tamper protection — a precursor step attackers take to persist undetected on endpoints (T1562.001 — Impair Defenses).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey has @"SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender"
    or RegistryKey has @"SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Features"
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet", "RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryValueName in~ ("DisableAntiSpyware", "DisableRealtimeMonitoring", "TamperProtection")
| extend AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: WMI Used for Lateral Execution
queries.description: Unexpected child processes spawned by WmiPrvSE.exe — WMI-based lateral execution technique that runs fileless on the target and bypasses many perimeter controls (T1047 — Windows Management Instrumentation).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "WmiPrvSE.exe"
| where FileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe", "SearchIndexer.exe", "WerFault.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: AD Group Membership Change — Specific Group Filter
queries.description: Surfaces all AD group membership changes for a specific group (default: PowerBI). Replace the group name to monitor any target group in real time.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityDirectoryEvents
| where Application == "Active Directory"
| where ActionType == "Group Membership changed"
| where AdditionalFields contains "PowerBI" // replace with the group name to monitor

queries.name: AS-REP Roasting — Accounts Without Kerberos Pre-Auth
queries.description: Detects TGT requests for accounts with pre-authentication disabled — AS-REP Roasting technique to obtain crackable hashes offline without requiring valid credentials (T1558.004).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityQueryEvents
| where QueryType == "Kerberos"
| where AdditionalFields has "AS-REQ"
| where AdditionalFields !has "PA-ENC-TIMESTAMP"
| summarize RequestCount = count() by AccountDisplayName, DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where RequestCount > 3
| order by RequestCount desc

queries.name: DCSync — Domain Controller Replication Simulation
queries.description: Detects accounts requesting DC replication with GetChangesAll permission — DCSync attack to extract all password hashes without touching the DC directly (T1003.006 — OS Credential Dumping: DCSync).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityDirectoryEvents
| where ActionType == "Directory Services Replication"
| where AdditionalFields has "GetChangesAll"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, DeviceName, TargetDeviceName, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Golden Ticket — TGT with Anomalous Lifetime
queries.description: Kerberos tickets with a lifetime exceeding company policy (typically 8–10h) may indicate a Golden Ticket forged with compromised KRBTGT credentials, granting unlimited access (T1558.001).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityLogonEvents
| where LogonType == "Network"
| where Protocol == "Kerberos"
| extend TicketLifetime = todouble(AdditionalFields.TicketLifetimeHours)
| where TicketLifetime > 10
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, DeviceName, DestinationDeviceName, TicketLifetime
| order by TicketLifetime desc

queries.name: Interactive Logon Success — Workstation Logons
queries.description: Filters domain logons to Interactive sessions only — physical console or local keyboard access. Useful for monitoring who is logging on locally to domain-joined machines.
queries.mitreNotApplicable: Generic interactive logon inventory with no threat filter
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityLogonEvents
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| extend DomainName = substring(DestinationDeviceName, indexof(DestinationDeviceName, '.') + 1)
| where DomainName contains "insidetechnologies.lcl" // replace with your domain
| summarize NumberOfEntries = count() by TimeGenerated, LogonType, ActionType, AccountDisplayName, DomainName, AccountSid, IPAddress, DeviceName, DC = DestinationDeviceName
| where LogonType contains "Interactive"
| sort by AccountDisplayName

queries.name: Kerberoasting — TGS Requests for Service Accounts
queries.description: Detects mass Kerberos TGS requests for service accounts with RC4 encryption — the Kerberoasting technique used to obtain crackable hashes for offline password attacks (T1558.003).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityQueryEvents
| where QueryType == "Kerberos"
| where AdditionalFields has "RC4"
| summarize RequestCount = count(), Services = make_set(TargetAccountDisplayName) by AccountDisplayName, DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where RequestCount > 5
| order by RequestCount desc

queries.name: LDAP Mass Enumeration — AD Reconnaissance
queries.description: Detects high-volume LDAP queries against Active Directory, typical of post-compromise discovery tooling (BloodHound, ldapdomaindump) that maps the environment before lateral movement (T1087 — Account Discovery).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityQueryEvents
| where QueryType == "Ldap"
| summarize QueryCount = count(), UniqueTargets = dcount(TargetAccountDisplayName) by AccountDisplayName, DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where QueryCount > 200
| order by QueryCount desc

queries.name: Logon Success — All Domain Logons
queries.description: Aggregates all successful identity logons in the domain, grouped by user, logon type, device, and DC. Useful as a baseline of normal logon activity to detect anomalies and unauthorized access.
queries.mitreNotApplicable: Baseline listing of successful domain logons, no threat filter
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityLogonEvents
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| extend DomainName = substring(DestinationDeviceName, indexof(DestinationDeviceName, '.') + 1)
| where DomainName contains "insidetechnologies.lcl" // replace with your domain
| summarize NumberOfEntries = count() by TimeGenerated, LogonType, ActionType, AccountDisplayName, DomainName, AccountSid, IPAddress, DeviceName, DC = DestinationDeviceName
| sort by AccountDisplayName

queries.name: Mass Member Removal from Privileged Groups
queries.description: Bulk removal of administrators from critical groups — sabotage tactic or preparation for an attack that reduces the number of active defenders (T1531 — Account Access Removal).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityDirectoryEvents
| where ActionType == "Group Membership changed"
| where AdditionalFields has "removed"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("Domain Admins", "Global Administrators", "IT Security")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, TargetAccountDisplayName, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: New Security Group Created in Active Directory
queries.description: Every new AD security group should be tracked — attackers create custom groups to grant persistent access or aggregate backdoor accounts without modifying existing privileged groups (T1136 — Create Account).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityDirectoryEvents
| where ActionType == "Group created"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, TargetAccountDisplayName, AdditionalFields, DeviceName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Pass-the-Hash — NTLM Auth from Unusual Workstations
queries.description: An account authenticating via NTLM from many different devices in a short period is a strong indicator of Pass-the-Hash, where stolen hashes are replayed across multiple hosts (T1550.002).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityLogonEvents
| where LogonType == "Network"
| where Protocol == "Ntlm"
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| summarize DevicesUsed = dcount(DeviceName), DeviceList = make_set(DeviceName) by AccountDisplayName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where DevicesUsed > 3
| order by DevicesUsed desc

queries.name: Pass-the-Ticket — Kerberos Access to Many Resources
queries.description: An account accessing more than 10 distinct resources via Kerberos within 30 minutes is a strong indicator of lateral movement using reused or forged tickets (T1550.003 — Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Ticket).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityLogonEvents
| where Protocol == "Kerberos"
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| summarize DistinctServices = dcount(DestinationDeviceName), ServiceList = make_set(DestinationDeviceName) by AccountDisplayName, bin(Timestamp, 30m)
| where DistinctServices > 10
| order by DistinctServices desc

queries.name: Password Spray — Many Accounts Failed from One IP
queries.description: Password spray attack pattern: the same source IP failing authentication against many distinct accounts in a short window to avoid per-account lockout policies (T1110.003 — Brute Force: Password Spraying).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityLogonEvents
| where ActionType == "LogonFailed"
| where LogonType in ("Network", "Interactive")
| summarize FailedAccounts = dcount(AccountDisplayName), AccountList = make_set(AccountDisplayName), AttemptCount = count() by IPAddress, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where FailedAccounts > 10
| order by FailedAccounts desc

queries.name: Security Group Deletion
queries.description: Deletion of security groups can remove access policies or protections — a high-impact action that should require formal change approval (T1531 — Account Access Removal).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityDirectoryEvents
| where ActionType == "Group deleted"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, TargetAccountDisplayName, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Sensitive Group Membership Changes (Configurable List)
queries.description: Detects additions and removals from a customizable list of sensitive AD groups (Domain Admins, IT, SQL, Veeam, etc.). Update the pack_array with your organization's privileged group names.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
let SensitiveGroupName = pack_array(
// Add your custom sensitive groups here
'Department ICT','Domain Admins','Enterprise Admins','Read-only Domain Controllers',
'Remote App ICT','SCCM Admins','SQL Admins','Veeam Backup Admins','Veeam Backup Operators Restore','Veeam Backup Operators View'
);
IdentityDirectoryEvents
| where Application == "Active Directory"
| where ActionType == "Group Membership changed"
| where isnotempty(DestinationDeviceName)
| extend ToGroup = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields)["TO_GROUP"])
| extend FromGroup = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields)["FROM_GROUP"])
| extend Action = iff(isempty(ToGroup), "Removed", "Add")
| extend GroupModified = iff(isempty(ToGroup), FromGroup, ToGroup)
| where GroupModified in~ (SensitiveGroupName)
| project Timestamp, Action, GroupModified,
    Target_Account = TargetAccountDisplayName, Target_UPN = TargetAccountUpn,
    DC = DestinationDeviceName, Actor = AccountDisplayName, ActorDomain = AccountDomain
| sort by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Suspicious Account Creation with Service-like Naming
queries.description: New accounts with names matching patterns of service or admin accounts (e.g. svc01, admin99, backup02) — attacker technique to create backdoor accounts that blend in with legitimate ones (T1136 — Create Account).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityDirectoryEvents
| where ActionType == "User Account created"
| where TargetAccountDisplayName matches regex @"(admin|svc|test|backup|support)\d{2,}"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, TargetAccountDisplayName, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Unexpected Addition to Privileged AD Groups
queries.description: Detects membership changes to critical Active Directory groups (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, etc.) — unauthorized escalation technique used by attackers to gain persistent privileged access (T1098 — Account Manipulation).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
IdentityDirectoryEvents
| where ActionType == "Group Membership changed"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("Domain Admins", "Enterprise Admins", "Schema Admins", "Administrators", "Account Operators")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, TargetAccountDisplayName, AdditionalFields, DeviceName
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: All Email from a Specific Sender Address
queries.description: Retrieves all emails from a specific address regardless of delivery outcome — starting point for any BEC or phishing investigation. Replace the placeholder with the address to investigate.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
EmailEvents
| where SenderFromAddress =~ "sender@domain.com" // replace with the address to investigate
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, SenderDisplayName, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, ThreatTypes, DetectionMethods
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: All Email from a Specific Sender Domain
queries.description: Aggregated view of all email from a suspicious domain — useful when investigating a campaign from an entire infrastructure rather than a single address.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
EmailEvents
| where SenderFromDomain =~ "suspicious-domain.com" // replace with the domain to investigate
| summarize EmailCount = count(), Recipients = make_set(RecipientEmailAddress), Subjects = make_set(Subject, 10) by SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, DeliveryAction
| order by EmailCount desc

queries.name: All Emails Classified as Malware by MDO
queries.description: Complete view of emails with malware payloads detected by Defender for Office 365 — includes blocked emails and any delivered before ZAP triggered.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
EmailEvents
| where ThreatTypes has "Malware"
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, ThreatTypes, DetectionMethods
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: All Emails Classified as Phishing by MDO
queries.description: Phishing emails detected by MDO — assess campaign volume, which users were targeted, and how many reached inboxes despite detection.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
EmailEvents
| where ThreatTypes has "Phish"
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, ThreatTypes, DetectionMethods
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Auto-Forward Rules to External Domains (BEC)
queries.description: Detects inbox or transport rules configured to silently forward email to external providers (Gmail, Yahoo, ProtonMail) — near-certain indicator of a compromised account used for BEC (T1114.003 — Email Forwarding Rule).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType in ("Set-MailboxAutoReplyConfiguration", "New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("ForwardTo", "ForwardAsAttachmentTo", "RedirectTo")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("gmail.com", "yahoo.com", "hotmail.com", "protonmail.com", "outlook.com")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, ActionType, AdditionalFields, IPAddress
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Bulk Mailbox Access — Mass Email Collection
queries.description: Detects a single account accessing more than 500 mailbox items in one hour — potential automated exfiltration via a non-managed client or OAuth token (T1114.002 — Remote Email Collection).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "MailItemsAccessed"
| where Application == "Microsoft Exchange Online"
| summarize MailsAccessed = count() by AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where MailsAccessed > 500
| order by MailsAccessed desc

queries.name: Delivered Emails with Suspicious TLD Links
queries.description: Identifies delivered emails containing URLs pointing to low-cost or ephemeral TLDs (.xyz, .top, .club, .tk, etc.) frequently used in phishing and C2 infrastructure (T1566.002 — Phishing: Spearphishing Link).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
EmailUrlInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| join kind=inner (
    EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(24h)
    | where DeliveryAction != "Blocked"
) on NetworkMessageId
| where UrlDomain matches regex @"\.(xyz|top|club|online|site|tk|ml|ga|cf)\b"
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, Url, UrlDomain
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Display Name Spoofing — External Sender Impersonating Internal User
queries.description: Emails where the visible display name matches an internal person but the domain is external — effective against users who only read the name, not the full address (T1566.001 — Spearphishing).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
let InternalDisplayNames = dynamic(["Mario Rossi", "Anna Bianchi", "CEO", "Amministratore", "IT Support", "Help Desk"]);
// replace with key people names in your organization
EmailEvents
| where SenderFromDomain != "insidetechnologies.it" // replace with your domain
| where SenderDisplayName in~ (InternalDisplayNames)
| project Timestamp, SenderDisplayName, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Email Keyword Search by Subject
queries.description: Finds emails containing specified keywords in the subject — locate all variants of a known phishing campaign or investigate a user-reported suspicious subject line.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
EmailEvents
| where Subject has_any ("fattura", "pagamento urgente", "verifica account", "reset password", "invoice", "wire transfer", "urgent payment")
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, ThreatTypes
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Emails Removed by Zero-Hour Auto Purge (ZAP)
queries.description: Emails initially delivered and later removed by ZAP — threat detected late; users may have already opened the message before removal.
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
queries.query:
EmailEvents
| where ThreatTypes has_any ("Malware", "Phish")
| where DeliveryAction == "Replaced"
    or LatestDeliveryAction == "ZAP"
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, ThreatTypes, DeliveryAction, LatestDeliveryAction, LatestDeliveryLocation
| order by Timestamp desc

queries.name: Emails with Links to External Cloud Storage
queries.description: External emails containing links to OneDrive, SharePoint, or Google Drive — growing technique to host malware or phishing pages on trusted infrastructure that bypasses email filters (T1566.002).
queries.author: Silvio Di Benedetto
